newsitem.title: ITALY: BancoNapoli sees return to profit in '98.
newsitem.headline: BancoNapoli sees return to profit in '98.

text.p: Banco di Napoli expects to break even in 1997 and return to profit in 1998, the bank's director general Federico Pepe told a shareholders' meeting.
Banco di Napoli uncovered record losses of 3.16 trillion lire in 1995 and plunged a further 1.65 trillion lire into the red last year, but was rescued from ruin by the government.
Pepe said last year's balance sheet was hit by 885 billion lire of extraordinary writedowns on the value of some holdings and 800 billion lire from downgrading the value of credits.
"Now all our activities are correctly valued. We might have some rectification of credits even over the next year, but certainly not on the same scale," Pepe told the assembly.
He added that this would not prevent a return to breakeven in 1997 followed by profits in 1998. "If possible we will try to do better," Pepe said.
He told shareholders that in the first three months of 1997, loans rose to 38.1 trillion lire from 37.9 trillion at the end of last year. Bad loans totalled 160 billion lire by the end of last month.
Client deposits remained stable at around 50.2 trillion lire, while money raised from services totalled 123 billion lire in the first quarter against 442 billion for the whole of 1996.
"The quality of our credits has improved," Pepe told the assembly. "Now the bank must take on the right risks."

He said Banco di Napoli was also looking into the possibility of selling some 27 branches in the centre and north of Italy. "This is a possibility, even if we have evaluated that some of this could be held onto," Pepe said.
Banco di Napoli sold many of its northern branches last year as part of a rescue package demanded by the government following the discovery of huge losses at the firm.
Insurer INA and Banca Nazionale del Lavoro are due to take a 60 percent stake in Banco di Napoli later this year. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
